overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic marine layer morning as of 11:45 ET (8:45 AM PT), with temperatures at 66.2°F under 100% cloud cover and a low ceiling of 549m — consistent with the NWS patchy fog advisory through 11 AM. The onshore southwest flow (5–15 mph) and high dewpoint (57.2°F) signal a marine-influenced day, with warming underway at +1.8°F/hr as the marine layer is expected to erode through midday.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS (71.6°F) and HRRR (71.5°F) align closely with the NWS forecast of ~71°F, while ECMWF (68.6°F) and NBM (67.2°F) run notably cooler, reflecting possible disagreement on how quickly and completely the marine layer clears. The ~4°F spread between the warmer and cooler model clusters introduces meaningful uncertainty; the cooler models may better capture persistent low cloud or the limiting effect of the onshore marine flow. The INTRADAY model's extreme-heat probabilities (90–106°F range) are physically implausible given current coastal conditions and should be disregarded.
max_temp_prediction: The META model — the most reliable signal here — places ~74% cumulative probability in the 70–73°F range, split evenly between the 70–71°F and 72–73°F buckets (~37% each), with meaningful downside risk toward 68–69°F (~15%). The NWS target of 71°F sits squarely in the center of this distribution and is well-supported by GFS and HRRR. Given the persistent marine influence, moderate onshore winds, and the slower-than-typical morning warm-up evident in hourly obs, a final high near 70–71°F is most likely, with confidence moderate — the cooler model cluster (ECMWF/NBM) cannot be dismissed if cloud clearing is delayed.
